name: Bangladesh Angels Network
applicationPath: Send a one-line company summary and PDF pitch deck through BAN's startup pitch form. Selected founders may be invited to a showcase and investor diligence.
notes: A member-led angel network that syndicates investments into early-stage, Bangladesh-linked digital businesses. BAN helps selected founders prepare their deck, data room and fundraising strategy before presenting them to angels for diligence and a common term sheet.

name: Bangladesh Women Investors Network
applicationPath: Submit a pitch through Bangladesh Angels Network's startup form; BWIN operates as BAN's gender-lens sister chapter.
notes: BAN's women-led sister chapter mobilises women angel investors and applies a gender lens to pre-seed and seed deals. It focuses on expanding capital, mentoring and investor access for women-led and women-focused ventures.

name: Startup Bangladesh Limited
chequeSize: BDT 25 lakh–5 crore per investment round
applicationPath: Complete Startup Bangladesh's online investment application with company, founder, traction and financial information.
notes: The ICT Division's government-owned venture-capital company invests equity or quasi-equity in Bangladesh-registered startups and impact enterprises with an MVP and evidence of customer or revenue growth. It can also provide governance and operational support and co-invest with other funders.

name: Anchorless Bangladesh
applicationPath: No public application route is published.
notes: A Bangladesh-focused early-stage fund investing primarily in seed rounds, with selective pre-seed and post-seed deals. It looks for companies with a technology or data advantage, scalable models, international expansion potential and a credible path to follow-on funding and exit.

name: Bangladesh Startup Investment Company PLC (BSIC)
applicationPath: Submit company and round details, a pitch deck and cap table through the BSIC: Deals form.
notes: A permanent venture-capital vehicle funded by 39 Bangladeshi commercial banks. Its US$35 million ONKUR fund is designed to co-invest in high-growth Bangladesh startups alongside a credible global or regional lead investor.

name: Dekko ISHO Venture Capital (DIVC)
applicationPath: Submit the startup and pitch deck through DIVC's rolling online application.
notes: A founder-focused venture investor backed by Dekko ISHO Group. It provides capital and hands-on support across strategy, operations, legal, hiring, branding and growth.

name: Bangladesh Venture Capital Limited (BVCL)
type: Venture capital investor and fund manager
applicationPath: Contact BVCL through its website with the business proposal and funding requirement.
notes: A Bangladesh venture-capital and alternative-investment company providing capital, mentorship, industry connections and strategic guidance to startups and growth-stage businesses.

name: YY Ventures
applicationPath: Email info@yy.ventures with a concise overview of the venture and its social or environmental impact.
notes: An impact investor and venture-support company for early-stage social businesses addressing challenges such as carbon emissions, poverty and unemployment in Bangladesh. It combines capital with hands-on help securing partners, customers and follow-on investors.

name: Accelerating Asia Ventures
chequeSize: US$100,000 upfront; up to US$150,000 in follow-on funding
applicationPath: Apply to the flagship accelerator through Accelerating Asia Ventures' Get Funded page; Cohort 14 applications are open.
notes: A Singapore-based VC accelerator investing in high-growth, pre-Series A technology startups across South and Southeast Asia. Investment is tied to its 100-day accelerator; participating companies pay a US$35,000 programme fee and give 3% equity, separate from the post-money SAFE investment terms.

name: IDLC Venture Capital
applicationPath: Applications are closed. IDLC says Fund I is exhausted and it is not currently investing. Follow the official application page for a future reopening.
notes: A Bangladesh-focused investor in early-stage technology and technology-enabled companies. Its published portfolio remains useful for research, but it is not a current funding route. The manager says it plans another fund in 2027; that is a plan, not an open call.
eligibility: Its published thesis targets scalable technology businesses solving problems in Bangladesh. New applications are currently closed.
